question.text:
An m × n real matrix A has matrices L and R satisfying LA = I and AR = I . Which must
n m
hold?
(A) m < n and L ̸= R
(B) m > n and L ̸= R
(C) m = n and L = R
(D) L = R but m and n may differ
(E) m = n but L and R may differ

solution.text:
The left-inverse equation forces rank A = n, and the right-inverse equation forces rank A =
m, so m = n. Associativity also gives L = L(AR) = (LA)R = R. Having both one-sided
inverses forces the unique two-sided inverse.
